column1: # Cross-shell contract scenarios. The ONE place a cross-shell behaviour gets a
# row: tests/bash/shell_contract.test.bash runs every row through the real Fish,
# Bash and Zsh integrations (tests/lib/shell_scenarios/render.*), each in its own
# sandbox, and requires the normalized prompt AND the observable side effects to
# be identical across the three shells.
# One scenario per line, TAB-separated. A cell is never empty: write `-`. The
# last five columns are optional; leave them off for a row against a live agent.
#   name  theme  segments  status  env  flags  agent  cwd  config  prime  expect
# name      unique label (SCN_FILTER=<regex> selects rows by it)
# theme     a theme in themes/ (copied into the sandbox), a built-in theme name,
#           or `variant-git` (the default theme with the git opening separator
#           read from the previous segment's colour, built by the harness)
# segments  comma-separated [ui] enabled_segments
# status    the previous command's exit status the prompt is rendered for
# env       space-separated KEY=VALUE pairs exported to the shell under test, or -
#           (HOME=, GPY_IPC_TIMEOUT_MS=150, GPY_GIT_INSTANT_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS=0 ...)
# flags     comma-separated, or -:
#             root                force the root-session flag
#             mask_seconds        the clock shows seconds, which differ between
#                                 the shells' samples of the time
#             drop_variants       after the `prime` render, delete every git
#                                 instant-cache entry but the context-free `.none`
#             down_after_prime    stop the agent after the `prime` render
#             aged_cache          backdate what the `prime` render cached by 5 s,
#                                 so it is older than a 1 s TTL
#             check_now           the drivers set the supervisor check interval
#                                 to 0, so every prompt runs the check
#             kill_after_first    the agent dies after the first prompt (the
#                                 harness kills its proxy and removes p.sock)
#             renders<N>          render N prompts in one shell process and
#                                 compare the last (state that spans prompts,
#                                 such as the script segment breaker); between
#                                 two prompts the driver simulates a command
#                                 (`SCN_BETWEEN`: an executable the harness may
#                                 place at <sandbox>/between.sh, run then)
# agent     up    the real agent, behind the recording IPC proxy (default)
#           down  no agent and no socket
#           slow  up, but a data request (git, directory, ...) is held 1.8 s
#                 before the agent sees it; register/ping/status are not
# cwd       `repo` (a scratch git repo with one commit), or an absolute path;
#           `-` is the checkout (default)
# config    extra config.toml text appended after [ui] ("\n" is a newline), or -.
#           The supervisor is off unless the text has an [agent.supervisor] table
# prime     segments of a throw-away render done first (so the instant cache
#           holds something), after which the observation log is cleared, or -
# expect    space-separated absolute checks applied to EACH shell, or -:
#             starts=N  oneshots=a,b|-  registers=N  ipc_total=N  ipc.<op>=N
#             other_calls=a,b|-   (the keys effects.py prints; an absent ipc.<op> is 0)
#             gpy_stderr=N   (stderr lines that start with `gpy:`)
#             prompt~=TEXT  prompt!~=TEXT   (normalized prompt contains / lacks TEXT)
# Side effects are what the shells did to the agent, seen from outside: `gpy-agent`
# invocations (start/restart are recorded but not performed; oneshot forks) and IPC
# requests by op, minus ping/status/unregister (see effects.py). A cross-shell
# difference fails the row even without an `expect`; `expect` pins the value so
# three shells that regress together fail too.
# Unprimed live-agent repo/git rows start with a verified-empty shell instant
# cache. Fixture setup first completes one unobserved real-agent git query and
# removes its instant entries, so the bounded render tests shell cold-miss
# behavior rather than cold daemon worker/cache setup speed under host load.
# Slow rows still impose their full 1.8 s delay on every observed data request.
# --- golden rows: shell-drawn clock, status, hostname, username, root prompt
ascii-ok
ascii-fail
ascii-local-session
ascii-status-only
ascii-status-first
ascii-status-last
ascii-root
ascii-root-fail-no-indicator
ascii-clock-24h-seconds
powerline-ok
powerline-fail
powerline-root
template-ok
template-fail
template-root
starship-flat
template-clock-12h-seconds
# Agent-rendered pills in first position: no opening cap, one leading space inside the pill
# (a token cannot hold a space, so `prompt!~=bg=X]'<content>` proves the content is not unpadded).
template-status-first
template-hostname-first
template-username-first
# --- behaviour rows: integration behaviour every shell must share
# agent disabled: the prompt still renders (oneshot), nothing is started or registered
disabled
# `[agent.supervisor] enabled=false` only gates restarts: the agent is still started
supervisor-off-down
# the agent dies between two prompts: the next checked prompt runs `start` once
restart-after-crash
# every start fails: the initial start plus max_restart_attempts retries
restart-cap
# cold git miss, agent down: the segment is omitted, no foreground `oneshot git`
cold-miss-down
# cold git miss, agent up: one bounded synchronous query
cold-miss-up
# variant fallback: a git entry for the wrong previous colour is corrected by one bounded sync query...
variant-up
# ...or, with the agent gone, the context-free entry is served as is
variant-down
# slow reply (connected, late): omitted, no oneshot fork, no resend. Two git requests
# are the sync query plus the one throttled background refresh a miss queues; a resend
# of the sync query would make it three.
slow-reply
# GPY_IPC_TIMEOUT_MS is honoured: a budget longer than the delay uses the late reply
ipc-timeout-long
# GPY_IPC_COLD_TIMEOUT_MS: with nothing to show (cold git cache, no directory memo) the
# prompt waits the cold budget, so a reply too late for GPY_IPC_TIMEOUT_MS still draws
cold-budget
# GPY_GIT_INSTANT_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS is honoured: a fresh entry is served with no git request...
ttl-fresh
# ...and an expired one is still drawn (stale) and the agent is asked to refresh it
ttl-expired
# empty HOME: the same prompt and requests with HOME= as with a home
empty-home
# agent disabled, two data segments: git is not omitted in any shell (it renders through oneshot, or
# draws nothing once the directory has spent the one-fork budget), so the directory is never the last segment
disabled-two-segments
# agent disabled, git alone: the segment renders through oneshot
disabled-git-only
# a theme without two_line (built-in `text`) draws the character on the segments' line in every shell
text-theme
# a newline in a segment format is a line break in every shell, rendered by oneshot, read from the instant cache, or answered live over IPC
multiline-oneshot
multiline-git-cached
multiline-directory-live
multiline-git-live
# --- script segments (fixture plugin contract-scripts), agent stopped: the shell runner draws them
# a script past its timeout_ms is hidden, as is one over the 4096-byte cap; the colour variant is styled
# the same in every shell; two timeouts in a row trip the breaker with one `gpy:` line
script-timeout
script-cap
script-variant
script-breaker
# --- env > config: an exported GPY_* user value wins over config.toml
# an exported GPY_AGENT_ENABLED=0 disables the agent even when config.toml enables it
env-disable-wins
# a prompt without `git` in ui.enabled_segments draws no git segment and the agent is never asked for git
# status (the export drops git from __enabled_segments, so no request is sent whatever the segment reader does)
env-git-unlisted
# the same for language (the wire op is `lang`; an absent ipc.<op> counts as 0, so ipc.language=0 would be vacuous)
env-language-unlisted
# positive control: with `git` listed the git segment draws
env-git-enabled
